creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The entire weighting of the script review ran off the invocation log and could not tell successes from failures. Every "N runs" figure in it counts attempts.

Worth adding at the same time: a foreground-child marker. `remind`'s day-long dialog children (up to 2.7 days) and `ct`'s 23-hour sessions skew every duration statistic derived from the log.

---

### Orientation

- The invocation log is written entirely by `core/logging_invocation.go`. `RegisterInvocationLogging()` installs a pre-exit callback (line 42); the callback builds an `InvocationLogEntry` and appends one JSON line.
- It is registered from `core/runner.go:72`, gated on `RConfig.InvocationLogging.Enabled` and `invocationType == ScriptFile`.
- The entry struct is `core/logging_invocation.go:45-52`: `epoch_millis`, `script_path`, `args` (omitempty), `rad_version`, `duration_millis`. No exit code, which is exactly the gap.
- Log location: `~/.rad/logs/invocations.jsonl` via `GetInvocationLogPath()`. Config type is `InvocationLoggingConfig` in `core/config.go`; user-facing docs are `docs-web/docs/guide/config.md`.

### Where to start

- **`core/exit.go` is the crux.** `RadExitHandler.Exit(code int)` (line 20) already stores the code in `h.codeToExitWith` *before* it runs the pre-exit callbacks (lines 33-42), so the value is available - it just is not passed. `AddPreExitCallback(cb func())` (line 48) takes a no-arg callback. Two options: widen the callback to `func(code int)`, or expose a getter on the handler. Widening is cleaner but touches every caller - `core/logging_invocation.go:42` and `core/defer.go:19` (`RegisterWithExit`) are the ones to check.
- Note the escalation logic at `core/exit.go:26-31`: a re-entrant `Exit` during deferred statements escalates a zero code to the error code. Log the final `codeToExitWith`, not the first one, or deferred-statement failures will be recorded as successes.
- **Reader side**: `core/funcs_internal_check_from_logs.go` parses this JSONL for `rad check --from-logs`. Any new field must be optional there, because existing log files will not have it.
- **Foreground-child marker**: children are run in `core/shell.go` (`cmd.Stdout` wiring at line 176, output collected at lines 227-236). Nothing currently records time spent in children. Whatever shape you pick - a boolean, or accumulated child-wall-time - it has to be accumulated in the shell layer and read in the pre-exit handler, which means new state reachable from `core/logging_invocation.go`.

### How to verify

```sh
make build
./bin/radd script.rad; echo "shell saw $?"
tail -3 ~/.rad/logs/invocations.jsonl
make test
```

Tests inject fakes for `RExit` and `RClock` (see `core/testing/test_helpers.go`), so the exit path is exercisable end to end without touching the real log file. `core/testing/shell_test.go` covers the shell layer.

### Done when

- A script exiting non-zero (uncaught error, explicit `exit(2)`, a failing critical shell command) records that code; a clean run records 0.
- A script whose deferred statements fail records the escalated code, not 0.
- `rad check --from-logs` still parses log files written by older versions - test with a hand-written line lacking the new field.
- `docs-web/docs/guide/config.md` documents the new field, since it documents the log's location and settings today.
- `make test` green.

### Watch out for

The zero-value trap. Adding a plain `ExitCode int` field with a `json:"exit_code"` tag makes "old line with no exit code" and "new line, exited 0" indistinguishable, which quietly re-creates the exact ambiguity this card exists to remove. Use a pointer (`*int`), or a distinct sentinel, and make the reader in `core/funcs_internal_check_from_logs.go` treat absence as unknown rather than success. Decide and document which.

Also: the callback only runs through `RadExitHandler.Exit`. Anything that bypasses it - a panic, a signal kill - writes no line at all. That is pre-existing behavior, but it means "attempts" and "logged runs" still will not match exactly, so do not promise the log is a complete record.
title: Record exit codes in the invocation log
